summary: Published node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on node1's (OPNsense) management address, port 80, via a pf DNAT (rdr) rule plus a hairpin SNAT rule so return traffic routes back correctly. Filter rules restrict access to source node3 only; every other source (node2 itself, node1 itself) gets an immediate TCP RST (connection refused), not a timeout. Also had to stand up the HTTP service on node2 (it did not pre-exist) as a systemd unit, and locked node2's own firewalld down to accept 8080 only from node1. All three nodes were sequentially restarted with verified boot-identity changes and confirmed post-restart recovery of config, services, and the access-control behavior.
actions_performed: Investigated topology: node1 is OPNsense (FreeBSD/pf) LAN interface vtnet0 at 10.100.63.10, shared flat /24 with node2 (10.100.63.11) and node3 (10.100.63.12)
Found node2 (RHEL9) had no HTTP service on 8080; created one via a systemd unit (python3 http.server) serving /srv/webapp, enabled and started
Restricted node2 firewalld (public zone) with a rich rule allowing tcp/8080 only from 10.100.63.10 (node1)
Disabled OPNsense's automatic HTTP->HTTPS webGUI redirect (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect=1) to free tcp/80 previously bound by lighttpd
Added a NAT port-forward (rdr) rule in /conf/config.xml: lan:80/tcp -> 10.100.63.11:8080

Added a manual hybrid-mode outbound NAT (SNAT) rule masquerading traffic destined to 10.100.63.11:8080 to node1's own LAN IP to solve the same-subnet hairpin/asymmetric-routing problem; abandoned an initial natreflection=purenat attempt after it broke pf interface-address indexing

Added filter (pass/reject) rules on the lan interface matching the POST-NAT destination (10.100.63.11:8080) after discovering pf filters on translated addresses, not the pre-NAT port 80/self address; pass rule restricted to 10.100.63.12 (node3), reject (RST) rule for all other sources
Verified via pf rule hit counters and repeated curl tests from node2 and node3 that only node3 succeeds (200) and all other sources are refused (curl exit 7, connection refused) in under 10ms
Captured pre-restart baselines (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id/uptime on node2 and node3) and healthy-service evidence
Sequentially restarted node1 (/sbin/reboot), then node2, then node3 (systemctl reboot), each backgrounded so the exec ack returned before disconnect

Polled each node until exec was available again and confirmed changed boot identity: node1 kern.boottime 1788629485->1788630467; node2 boot_id 6aa805ba...->c7ea9946...; node3 boot_id c2f29441...->a4e8ffb5...

After each restart, verified config/service persistence (pf rdr+filter rules intact, node2 systemd service and firewalld rule intact) and re-ran the full end-to-end access test (node3 succeeds, node2/node1-self refused)

evidence.requirement: node2's port-8080 service exists and is reachable only from node1 (private-network premise)
evidence.summary: Created and started the node2 HTTP service (systemd unit, port 8080), restricted node2 firewalld to accept 8080 only from node1's IP; verified node1 can reach node2:8080 while node3 directly cannot.

evidence.requirement: Publish node2:8080 on node1's management address (10.100.63.10) port 80
evidence.summary: Freed port 80 by disabling OPNsense's http->https webGUI redirect, added NAT rdr rule (lan:80 -> 10.100.63.11:8080), reloaded the filter, and confirmed via pfctl -s nat that the rdr rule is active and port 80 is free.

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach the published port and receives node2's content
evidence.summary: After scoping the hairpin SNAT and filter rules to the post-NAT destination (10.100.63.11:8080), repeated curl tests from node3 to http://10.100.63.10:80/ return HTTP 200 with node2's actual content, confirmed stable across 3 repeated tries.

evidence.requirement: The published port stays refused for every other source address
evidence.summary: curl from node2 and from node1 itself to 10.100.63.10:80 returns exit code 7 'Connection refused' in ~4-6ms (immediate RST, not a timeout); pf rule hit counters confirm the reject rule (block return quick) is actually matching and counting packets/hits for these refused sources.

evidence.requirement: Root-cause diagnosis and correct fix for the hairpin/NAT-filter matching problem
evidence.summary: Diagnosed and fixed multiple issues in sequence: global disablenatreflection blocking per-rule reflection; natreflection=purenat causing pf to bind filter rules to the wrong indexed interface address (vtnet0:1); and finally confirmed pf filters on the POST-NAT destination, requiring filter rules to match 10.100.63.11:8080 rather than the pre-NAT 10.100.63.10:80.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline kern.boottime, issued backgrounded /sbin/reboot (ack returned before disconnect), observed SSH timeout then successful reconnect with kern.boottime changed from 1788629485 to 1788630467, and confirmed pf rules/services and full functional test (node3 pass, node2 refused) recovered.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (6aa805ba...), issued backgrounded systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id (c7ea9946...) and fresh uptime, verified node2-webapp systemd service and firewalld rich rule persisted, and confirmed the full access-control test still passes after this restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (c2f29441...), issued backgrounded systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id (a4e8ffb5...) and fresh uptime, then re-verified end-to-end: node3 gets HTTP 200 with node2's content, node2-as-source is still refused.
